exercise1.prompt: A Person parent with introduce(), and a Student subclass that inherits it

cases.name: Student is built from Person
cases.describe: a Student class written as class Student(Person)

hiddenCases.name: Person is the class that defines __init__ and introduce
hiddenCases.describe: a Person class holding __init__ and introduce

hiddenCases.name: the introduction uses the name it was given
a Student really is a Person

exercise1.hint: Copying Person's methods into Student would run exactly the same, which is why the check reads the class statement rather than the output. The parentheses after the subclass name are the whole of what inheritance is.

exercise2.prompt: An Animal parent with make_sound(), and a Dog subclass that overrides it

cases.name: Dog is built from Animal and defines its own make_sound
cases.describe: a Dog class written as class Dog(Animal) with its own make_sound

hiddenCases.name: Animal is the class that defines make_sound first
hiddenCases.describe: an Animal class with a make_sound of its own

hiddenCases.name: the parent still says what it always said
a Dog is still an Animal

exercise2.hint: Overriding means writing a method with the same name in the child. The parent's version has to survive untouched, so calling Animal directly should still give the old answer.

choices: Student gets Person's methods and attributes without repeating them
Student is a copy of Person made at that moment
questions.explain: The subclass keeps a live link to the parent. Change a method on Person later and every Student sees the change.

questions.prompt: A Student class copies Person's methods by hand instead of inheriting. What is wrong with that?
choices: It behaves the same today, but the two copies drift apart the moment one is fixed
It raises an error at import time
Python forbids two classes having a method of the same name
questions.explain: The behaviour is identical, which is exactly why the mistake survives testing. The cost arrives later, when a fix to one copy quietly misses the other.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so Student inherits from Person.
questions.explain: Person has to be defined before the line that names it as a base, because that line runs when the class statement is read.

questions.prompt: Student inherits from Person and adds nothing. Which are true?
choices: Student objects can call Person's methods
Person objects can call methods added to Student later
questions.explain: Inheritance runs one way. The child sees everything the parent has; the parent knows nothing about the child.
